PF-E5088.message: The branches of this {kind} return incompatible types: one returns a value and another returns nothing.
PF-E5088.hint: Give every branch a value, or call the void function as a separate statement.
PF-E5088.explanation: TradingView refuses a consumed if or switch with a value arm and a terminal void arm (CE10235). Statement selections, implicit missing arms and selections whose present arms all return values or all return nothing retain their existing behavior.
PF-E5088.user_message: The branches of this {kind} must all return compatible values.

PF-E5089.message: {function}: TradingView refuses keyword arguments for functions with a variable number of arguments.
PF-E5089.explanation: TradingView refuses every keyword argument on variadic math functions; supply their arguments by position.

PF-E5090.message: {function}: unknown keyword argument ''{name}''; accepted keyword names: {accepted}.
PF-E5090.explanation: The math function does not declare this keyword; use the parameter names recorded for that function.

PF-W1505.message: ta.ema seeds from the first value of the data PineForge runs, so it can differ from TradingView at the start of a run whose reference started where your range starts.
PF-W1505.hint: The first-value seed matches TradingView when its chart had history before your range, and the difference has decayed by then. If your TradingView reference starts at your range start, declare it: set series_origin_ms to the open time of its first bar (a run option, passed through syminfo). The indicator is then na for the first length-1 bars and starts from the SMA of the first length bars, as TradingView does. The same holds for ta.macd and ta.tsi; ta.kc and ta.kcw already start that way in every run. Declaring it also starts request.security series at the first whole higher-timeframe bucket at or after that time, and a plain security expression stays na until the first higher-timeframe bar completes.
PF-W1505.explanation: By default, ta.ema seeds from the first value, matching charts with prior history. With series_origin_ms at the reference range start, it is na for length-1 bars, then seeds from the SMA. This also applies to ta.macd and ta.tsi; ta.kc, ta.kcw, ta.rsi, ta.rma and ta.atr already use SMA seeds.
